cita: Ye, C., Liu, Y., Wang, Y., Yu, H., Zhao, Y., Liu, G., McAuley, J. y You, J. (2026). Auto-Dreamer: Learning Offline Memory Consolidation for Language Agents.
problema: Existing language-agent memory systems couple fast per-session acquisition and slow cross-session consolidation into a single online update, so they cannot discover recurring patterns, abstract reusable procedures, resolve contradictions, or prune redundant entries across sessions.
mecanismo: Two-timescale design: a fixed local append-only writer records typed entries per session; a learned offline consolidator (GRPO-trained, Qwen3-14B) performs a bounded tool-use rollout over a selected working region R (search/inspect/get-source-trace), treating R as read-only provenance-grounded evidence and synthesizing a replacement set S that supersedes R (region rewriting), rewarded by downstream task utility plus a counterfactual-masking term that credits load-bearing entries and penalizes redundant ones.
evaluacion: Continual-memory deployment and fixed-bank consolidation on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld and WebArena, benchmarked against 10 baselines across 7 families (Reflexion, ExpeL, AWM, Memp, ReasoningBank, Mem0, LightMem, Mem-alpha, UMEM), reporting success rate, AUC and active memory-bank token size, plus ablations isolating region rewriting and the counterfactual reward.
numeros_clave: ScienceWorld 41.1% SR (+7pts vs UMEM 34.1%) with 12x smaller memory bank than the strongest baseline; ALFWorld 60.2% SR with 6x less memory; WebArena 52.3% SR leading all baselines; fixed-bank ALFWorld 72.7% acc using only 634 tokens vs Memp 927 / ReasoningBank 3,221.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: A learned offline consolidator achieves large measured token compaction (12x/6x, Table 1) while improving task success, a concrete write-side lever for MF's context-economy goal.
Region-rewriting replace-semantics (§4.1: old entries persist only if re-synthesized into S) is a directly adoptable pattern for promoting transient gotchas into durable recipes.
Consolidation is provenance-grounded (re-readable source trajectories linked from every entry, Fig.1), supporting MF's stance that consolidated memory must stay traceable to source.

notes: Numbers anchored in Table 1 (continual deployment + fixed-bank panels) and §4.1-4.3 (region-rewriting formalism, Eq.1-2); Fig.2 gives the full architecture.

cita: Bi et al. (2025). Real-Time Procedural Learning From Experience for AI Agents.
problema: LLM-based agents lack a posteriori mechanisms to acquire procedural knowledge after deployment; a priori written SOPs are incomplete (humans learn by observation, not documentation), cannot enumerate all edge cases, and go stale as web interfaces change.
mecanismo: PRAXIS writes a state-action-result tuple after every action in real time: pre-action environment state, agent internal state/goal, action taken, post-action environment state. Retrieval (Alg.1) jointly matches environment-state similarity (IoU + length overlap) to select a top-k candidate set, then re-ranks by internal-state embedding similarity and a threshold, injecting matched exemplars into the action-selection node of the Altrina web agent.
evaluacion: REAL web-browsing benchmark (11 site replicas, 112 tasks) across five VLM backbones (Llama4, Qwen3-VL, Gemini2.5 Flash, GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4.5), measuring accuracy, best-of-5 accuracy, reliability (success rate over 5 repeats) and steps-to-completion, with an ablation over retrieval breadth k.
numeros_clave: Average accuracy 40.3%->44.1% with procedural memory; best-of-5 53.7%->55.7%; reliability 74.5%->79.0%; steps-to-completion 25.2->20.2; accuracy rises monotonically then plateaus as retrieval breadth k grows (Fig.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Retrieval is a measured joint state+goal similarity policy with an explicit breadth-k ablation (Fig.3, §4.4), a concrete alternative measured-retrieval design MF could compare against ADR-019's stance.
The write trigger is every single action step (append-only, real time, §3.2), an aggressive discretionary-write baseline MF's G-M1 design could be measured against.

notes: Fig.1-3 and Table 1-2 (REAL benchmark, per-backbone deltas) anchor the numbers; Altrina is an industry proprietary agent (formerly Tessa), single benchmark family.

cita: Omelchenko, I. y Strukov, V. (2025). Reflective memory architecture for adaptive planning in hierarchical LLM agents in virtual environments.
problema: Storing the complete interaction history for LLM-based planning agents overflows the context window, raises computational cost and planning latency, and degrades attention performance, so agents need a bounded inter-episode memory mechanism.
mecanismo: A Reflective Memory System evolves a typed set of RULE memory elements (content + importance score, init 0.5) via LLM-generated CRUD-like operators (CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE/CONFIRM) applied every k episodes by a larger reflecting LLM (Qwen3:30b); importance is updated by an exponential moving average from DELETE/CONFIRM signals, and elements below a threshold are pruned, while a smaller planner LLM (Qwen3:8b) consumes the surviving rules.
evaluacion: Ablation across 9 memory configurations (no memory, episodic-only, offline reflection, three unstructured-reflection variants, structured Reflection every 2/5 episodes, manual expert instructions) in the Minigrid ColoredDoorKey environment, measured by task accuracy, cumulative reward, steps-per-episode and planning duration/cost.
numeros_clave: Structured Reflection E-2 reaches accuracy 0.99 (reward 0.7353, 29.29 steps) vs the no-memory baseline's 0.68 (reward 0.4994, 52.06 steps), matching or exceeding the Manual-Instructions upper bound (0.99, reward 0.7345) (Table 1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: CRUD reflection operators with importance-score decay and pruning (§3.3) empirically beat naive full-history accumulation, supporting MF's promotion-of-gotchas-to-recipes consolidation design.
The paper explicitly measures Planning Duration as a function of memory size (Table 1's step/latency metrics), backing MF's concern that unbounded memory growth raises inference cost.

notes: Table 1 (9-config comparison) and §3.3 (CRUD operator equations) anchor the numbers; single small environment (Minigrid) and niche student-thesis venue (Karazin Kharkiv bulletin) -- RECONSIDERAR generalizability of the ablation.

cita: Lin et al. (2026). MUSE-Autoskill: Self-Evolving Agents via Skill Creation, Memory, Management, and Evaluation.
problema: Prior automatic-skill systems (Voyager, AutoSkill, EvoSkill, SkillGen, Anthropic Agent Skills) cover only part of the skill lifecycle: they lack structured per-skill memory, unit-test-driven evaluation/refinement, or handle long-horizon context poorly, leaving skills as static, unvalidated artifacts.
mecanismo: MUSE unifies five lifecycle stages -- creation, memory, management, evaluation, refinement -- around a built-in skill_create tool invoked inside the agent's ReAct loop: new skills are packaged as SKILL.md+scripts/tests/resources, gated by a create->evaluate->register loop that runs unit tests/sandbox checks and triggers a Refiner on failure; multi-level memory adds skill-level per-skill .memory.md notes atop short-term (compressed) and long-term (persistent) memory; management does catalog-based retrieval, merging of overlapping skills and pruning of unused ones.
evaluacion: SkillsBench (75-task, 4 super-domains, Docker-graded verifiers) and SkillLearnBench (100-instance continual-skill benchmark), compared against Hermes, Codex and Claude Code (all GPT-5.5-backed), with/without human- or self-authored skills, plus a cross-agent transfer experiment and a run-to-run stability analysis.
numeros_clave: SkillsBench human-skill average 59.67% (+12.72pp lift); self-created-skill accuracy 53.42% vs Codex 47.52% and Claude Code 44.27%; self-created skills beat human skills on the covered subset (85.24% vs 81.17%); transfer to Hermes reaches 51.90% (exceeds Hermes+human 48.02%); SkillLearnBench human/self-created 72.0%/48.0%.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The skill-management stage's merge/prune/refine over a growing skill bank (§3.2) is a directly transferable pattern for promoting durable, testable procedures in MF.
The structured context manager provides adaptive compression with cross-session state persistence for long-horizon tasks (§3.4), directly relevant to treating plan/task state as first-class memory.
Skills are unit-test/sandbox-gated before registration (create->evaluate->register loop, §3.2), confirming MF's stance that consolidated artifacts need a validation gate against drift.

notes: SkillsBench Fig.1/Table 2-3 anchor the accuracy numbers; §3.4 (context manager, cross-session state) anchors the PLAN-ESTADO claim; skill format follows Anthropic's Agent Skills spec (§3.2).

cita: Liu et al. (2026). MemPro: Agentic Memory Systems as Evolvable Programs.
problema: Existing agentic memory systems typically adapt only the memory bank or its prompt text while keeping the surrounding memory-construction-retrieval (MCR) pipeline fixed after deployment, so they struggle with heterogeneous task-specific failure modes and drift out of alignment as the bank evolves.
mecanismo: MemPro treats the entire MCR pipeline (both prompts and executable code) as the evolution target, maintaining a version tree of runnable pipeline implementations with per-node evaluation logs; an Evolving Agent iteratively selects a promising node, diagnoses recurring failure modes from the logs, and expands it via a sequence of EDIT/DEBUG/TERMINATE actions (failure-mode-guided edit-debug refinement) to produce an improved child pipeline version, which is then evaluated on a held-out training split.
evaluacion: LongMemEval, LoCoMo, HotpotQA (56K/224K/448K context lengths) and NarrativeQA, compared against static agentic memory baselines (Mem0, A-MEM, MemoryOS, LightMem, GAM, etc.) and prompt-only evolution (GEPA, MetaMem), with an ablation removing code-level edits, the version tree, and iterative expansion.
numeros_clave: MemPro-15 LongMemEval avg 79.00 vs best baseline GAM 72.40 (gpt-4o-mini); LoCoMo avg rises 79.48->84.93 from MemPro-5 to MemPro-15; HotpotQA avg F1 66.72 vs GAM 61.50; ablation removing code-level edits drops LoCoMo score from 84.93 to ~74.83 (Fig.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Evolving the whole MCR pipeline as one runnable, versioned artifact (rather than only its data store) is a pattern relevant to MF's single-source-per-fact / multi-store-seams question.

The paper claims a 'favorable performance-cost trade-off' (abstract, Fig.1 iteration curve) but reports no explicit token/latency ablation table, so it is context without a hard cost number for MF to act on.

notes: Table 1-2 (main benchmark results) and Fig.3 (ablation, w/o Code drops ~10pts) anchor the numbers; version-tree evolution operates over executable pipeline code, not memory content itself.

cita: Wang et al. (2026). Learning to Retrieve: Dual-Level Long-Term Memory for Text-to-SQL Agents.
problema: Memory retrieval for interactive text-to-SQL agents either uses fixed similarity heuristics that ignore downstream utility, or single-horizon dynamic retrieval trained only from sparse terminal rewards at the episode level, mismatching interactions where useful memory differs between initial planning and local, state-conditioned execution.
mecanismo: MERIT maintains two memory banks: episode-level memory (full trajectories + distilled insights) retrieved via embedding candidates plus an RL-trained (PPO) selector trained on terminal reward for global strategy, and turn-level memory (state-signature-indexed state-action-observation snippets) retrieved via a second RL-trained selector; because turn-level retrieval lacks direct outcome labels, a lightweight Process Reward Model (SFT+GRPO on teacher rubrics) scores retrieved-memory utility per turn and supplies dense PPO rewards.
evaluacion: BIRD-Interact (in-domain, Phase1/Phase2, READ/WRITE task splits) against no-memory, static-retrieval (BM25, cosine similarity, TopicK) and dynamic-retrieval (Memento, MemRL) baselines, plus zero-shot transfer to Spider2-Snow and ablations on component removal, retrieval breadth (pass@k) and retrieved-memory count.
numeros_clave: MERIT overall success 33.01% Phase1 / 22.17% Phase2 (best baseline TopicK/Memento reach 27.17%/16.00% and 29.00%/18.83%); lowest avg turns 7.84 (Phase2) vs No-Memory 8.93; Spider2-Snow transfer 69.29% vs No-Memory 66.00%; removing episode-level memory drops Phase1 success to 23.50% (Table 3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: A dense Process-Reward-Model score, not embedding similarity alone, drives turn-level retrieval training (§5.3), reinforcing MF's ADR-019 stance that retrieval quality should be measured/learned, not assumed.
MERIT lowers average interaction turns relative to no-memory and every baseline (Table 1), evidence that better-targeted dual-horizon retrieval reduces operational cost, not just improves accuracy.

notes: Table 1 (BIRD-Interact Phase1/2) and Table 2 (Spider2-Snow transfer) anchor the numbers; the episode-vs-turn dual-horizon split is the key differentiator vs the single-horizon Memento/MemRL baselines.
